correctness.rationale: For the scalar pair with coefficients 2^{-j} and 2^{1-j}, every weaving has exact energy between one third and four thirds. If one square-summable reconstruction sequence worked for every partition, toggling a single index would force its coefficient to vanish; doing this at every index contradicts reconstruction. For the positive theorem, the uniform lower bound is equivalent to C K K* less than or equal to T_sigma T_sigma*, and Douglas factorization gives K=T_sigma U_sigma with norm squared at most 1/C. Coordinate projections of U_sigma form the required partition-dependent family. The converse follows from K*=U_sigma* T_sigma* and the uniform Bessel norm.

final_claim: Wovenness of two K-g-frames does not imply one common Bessel reconstruction family valid for every partition. A scalar geometric pair gives a counterexample. The exact uniform replacement is that each partition may have its own reconstruction family, with one Bessel bound uniform over partitions; this is equivalent to a uniform weaving lower bound.
